Gurdwara Jhari Sahib, (Gurmukhi: ਗੁਰੂਦਵਾਰਾ ਝਾੜੀ ਸਾਹਿਬ; Shahmukhi: ) is a gurdwara situated on the outskirts of a village named  Tergay, in the district of Kasur in Punjab, Pakistan. The gurdwara is located about 1.8km from the border between Pakistan and India, on the Kasur-Qadiwind road.
History
Guru Amar Das' visit to Tergay Village
According to many historical accounts Guru Amar Das Ji, the third guru of Sikhism, visited the area of what is modern-day Kasur district. The villagers welcomed him, and urged him to stay. He agreed, and  a small gurdwara was built there.  During his stay, Guru Amar Das tied his horses to the trees nearby, which have now withered away. The gurdwara was mentioned in many scriptures until 1930, and it was also known as Agadhi Pachadi Sahib.
Deterioration of the Gurdwara's pillars
In recent years, the gurdwara's pillars were severely deteriorating, posing a risk of collapse. Major Sikh organisations urged the Pakistani Punjabi government to restore the pillars and prevent the collapse of a gurdwara in Pakistan with a history regarding Guru Amar Das, who is a major person in Sikhism. The gurdwara has been referred to as an 'important cultural and historical landmark.'
Restoration of the Pillars and current status
Around November 2025, The Punjabi Government approved the restoration of the pillars of Gurdwara Jhari Sahib. The pillars were rebuilt with new bricks.
Every year on Vaisakhi a fair is held.  The gurdwara lays in an open field and is currently considered abandoned. The Gurdwara had five ghumaons of land in its name,  which 2.5 ghumaon (roughly 1.01 hectares) went to Bhai Sulakhan Singh of Qadiwind and the other 2.5 ghumaon to the locals by the Gurdwara.
